messages:
ben_acme: Hi team — reporting a weird session problem after MFA re-enrollment. Customer re-enrolled MFA on a new phone and now every subsequent request from their iOS in-app webview returns 401. Token exchange returns `invalid_grant`. Happened after the MFA step completed. Happening for a subset of users on iOS 15/16 webviews.

emma_support: Thanks @ben_acme. Can you share repro steps and a request/response log (redact tokens)? Also which flow are you using (OAuth web flow / PKCE / API key)?

ben_acme: Using standard OAuth PKCE (redirect back to app webview). Steps: 1) Login on desktop (works) 2) On mobile, trigger re-enroll MFA (user scans new device) 3) After re-enroll, returning to app webview shows UI logged out, network calls 401.

ben_acme: Quick curl of failing call (redacted):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sessions/refresh \
  -H "Origin: https://app.acme.com" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -b "session=eyJ...(redacted)..." \
  -d '{"refresh_token":"(redacted)"}'
```

emma_support: Got it. Pinging SRE and ProdSec to look at token revocation and cookie flags. @raj_sre @lena_prodsec any immediate ideas? :eyes:

raj_sre: Looking at logs for ben_acme org around 2026-03-15T15:10Z. I see refresh token rotation events that coincide with MFA re-enroll. We rotate refresh tokens on MFA changes for device trust reasons (we revoke previous refresh tokens). When the client holds an old refresh token but the server has already rotated/revoked it, the token exchange fails with `invalid_grant`.

raj_sre: However that alone wouldn't explain the webview behavior where the cookie isn't sent on certain requests. I pulled a failing trace: request has no Cookie header when coming from the in-app webview after the redirect. Same user in Safari shows the cookie present.

lena_prodsec: Two possible vectors: 1) refresh token revocation on re-enroll (expected) 2) SameSite cookie policy + webview redirect causing cookie not to be sent across the redirect boundary. On iOS webviews the redirect from `oauth.redwood.ai -> app.acme.com` can be treated as cross-site and Lax/SameSite default would block cookie on POSTs.

emma_support: Can you paste the Set-Cookie header we currently set for session?

raj_sre: Currently our response sets:
```
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Domain=.redwood.ai; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
```

lena_prodsec: Lax will not send the cookie on a cross-site POST triggered by a third-party webview redirect. For webviews we need `SameSite=None; Secure` so the cookie will be included when the app navigates back after MFA. But we must be careful and audit CSRF protections.

ben_acme: So is the permanent fix to change SameSite? That seems risky but would fix our users immediately.

emma_support: Two-pronged path: short term, suggest customers clear cookies and force a fresh sign-in after MFA re-enroll — that will obtain a fresh refresh token + cookie. Long term, we should evaluate changing cookie flags conditionally for SDK/webview flows.

raj_sre: Agreed. I can add telemetry for `refresh_token_revoked_due_to_mfa` and `missing_cookie_on_redirect` to quantify impact. Also propose a canary to set `SameSite=None` for `Set-Cookie` on our oauth endpoints for requests that include `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate` + `User-Agent` matching known in-app webviews. We'll need ProductSec signoff.

lena_prodsec: I'm +1 for a targeted canary (small percentage) and only for endpoints used by OAuth redirect flows. We'll also require CSRF double submit for POST endpoints if SameSite is relaxed.

emma_support: For the customer: recommend this temporary workflow: 1) Clear in-app webview cookies (or instruct users to open a system browser) 2) Sign-in again (fresh PKCE flow) 3) If issue persists, collect a HAR (if possible) or `curl -v` output showing missing Cookie header and open a support ticket.

ben_acme: I'll push an update to our in-app flow so we open the system browser for auth and not the embedded webview as immediate workaround. Thanks.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canaried config change scheduled: cookie.same_site override = None for 2% of oauth traffic. Change id: cfg-20260315-42. Rollout window: 2026-03-16 02:00-03:00 UTC.

raj_sre: Action items: - raj_sre: add telemetry and log filter for `refresh_token_revoked_due_to_mfa` (ETA 4h) - lena_prodsec: review CSRF mitigations and approve narrow canary (ETA EOD) - emma_support: send customer-facing steps & wording and mark ticket P2 (ETA 30m)

emma_support: Will send a concise message to Ben with exact steps and link to our recommended workaround. Also asked them to capture `curl -v` if they run into it again.

ben_acme: Thanks all — will follow up after we switch to system browser flow. Appreciate the quick triage. :pray:
